claims.text: The 428 status code indicates that the origin server requires the request to be conditional.

Its typical use is to avoid the "lost update" problem, where a client GETs a resource's state, modifies it, and PUTs it back to the server, when meanwhile a third party has modified the state on the server, leading to a conflict.

claims.text: The 431 status code indicates that the server is unwilling to process the request because its header fields are too large.
It can be used both when the set of request header fields in total is too large, and when a single header field is at fault.

rows.notes: Corrected signal now resolves 431 rather than old 429; reason and optional retry supported.

claims.text: The Content-Type header of a POST or BREW request sent to a TEA-capable pot MUST be "message/teapot" if tea is to be requested.

rows.notes: Root URI does not commence brewing; Alternates MUST preserved, quoted header options match.

claims.text: For the "/" URI, brewing will not commence; instead, an Alternates header as defined in RFC 2295 MUST be sent, with the available tea bags and/or leaf varieties as entries.

rows.notes: 300 is RECOMMENDED, never mandatory. Root choices, not brewing, preserved.

claims.text: A BREW request to the "/" URI will return an Alternates header indicating the URIs of the available varieties of tea to brew, and it is RECOMMENDED that this response be served with a status code of 300, to indicate that brewing has not commenced and further options must be chosen by the client.

rows.notes: MAY and condition concerning unacceptable additions both preserved.

claims.text: Services that implement the Accept-Additions header field MAY return a 403 status code for a BREW request of a given variety of tea, if the service deems the combination of additions requested to be contrary to the sensibilities of a consensus of drinkers regarding the variety in question.

rows.notes: Not provisioned to brew coffee condition and alternatives 503 temporary/418 more permanent preserved.

claims.text: TEA-capable pots that are not provisioned to brew coffee may return either a status code of 503, indicating temporary unavailability of coffee, or a code of 418 to denote a more permanent indication that the pot is a teapot.

rows.notes: Continuation refers to preceding two codes for unprovisioned coffee; 503 temporary matches the quote.

claims.text: A status code of 503 indicates temporary unavailability of coffee.

rows.notes: The other code correctly refers to 418; more permanent is relative, not an invented unconditional prohibition.

claims.text: A code of 418 denotes a more permanent indication that the pot is a teapot.

rows.notes: ABNF sugar-type alternatives establish Sugar/Xylitol/Stevia; quotation and section identify HTCPCP-TEA.

claims.text: HTCPCP-TEA adds the sugar-type values "Sugar", "Xylitol" and "Stevia".

rows.notes: Equivalence to BREW and deprecation both stated by quoted section.

claims.text: POST requests are treated equivalently to BREW requests, but they remain deprecated.

rows.notes: BREW body stop BEFORE recommended strength triggers MUST abort and weaker beverage, preserving all conditions.

claims.text: If a BREW command with an entity body containing "stop" is received before the recommended strength is achieved, the pot MUST abort brewing and serve the resultant beverage at lesser strength.
